name: The Multisecular Beech of Saint-Jammes

location.address: D45 road between Sorèze and Arfons, beside the ruins of the pre-Romanesque Chapelle de Saint-Jammes, Montagne Noire, Sorèze, Tarn, Occitania, France

access: Free, unenclosed rural site on the D45 between Sorèze and Arfons; only the trunk itself carries a light protective fence and two branches are propped. No gate, no ticket, open ground.
transport: Rural Montagne Noire, no public transport; reached by car or on foot/bike via the D45, roughly 8km from Sorèze centre.
verify_notes: Contest source and the town of Sorèze's own page (ville-soreze.fr) agree on all facts: 450 years old, 20m tall, 6m trunk circumference (girth_cm=600), 90m canopy diameter. Stands beside the ruins of an 11th-century pre-Romanesque chapel and an old cemetery, on the former Prats Vieils estate, a stop on the Way of St James to Compostela. Won 'Remarkable Tree of the Year 2019' from French association A.R.B.R.E.S. before placing 11th in European Tree of the Year 2020 (12,192 votes). Site of local legend/pilgrimage tradition. GPS: contest's own DMS coordinate (43.434692, 2.112808) and an independent OSM node for 'Ruines de la Chapelle de Saint-Jammes' (43.435164, 2.112753) agree within about 50 metres, both placing the chapel ruins the tree stands beside; used the OSM figure. Good single-famous-tree candidate: named, specific site, real girth and story, remote rural location with essentially nothing else nearby to build a 'place' around beyond this tree and the chapel ruins.

name: The Old Mulberry of Veliki Preslav

location.address: Public garden with fountain, town centre of Veliki Preslav, Shumen Region, Bulgaria

access: Free, in a public garden/square with a fountain in the centre of Veliki Preslav; a community gathering spot, open ground with no restrictions.
transport: Small town centre, walkable from anywhere in Veliki Preslav; no metro or rail, reached by road (Veliki Preslav is on route 73/E772 between Shumen and Zavet, roughly 20km from Shumen).
verify_notes: Age (~450 years) and species (white mulberry / Morus alba) confirmed by two independent Bulgarian sources beyond the contest page: news.bg (2020, on winning the Bulgarian 'Tree with Roots' contest) and bnr.bg (Radio Bulgaria, on the European Tree of the Year 2021 entry, 30,055 votes, placed 14th). Local legend: national revolutionary Stefan Karadzha reportedly hid from Ottoman authorities in a pub beside the tree; the tree is also linked by local tradition to Vasil Levski and to a 1900 visit by writer Ivan Vazov, who reportedly met townspeople at a cafe under its branches. No source anywhere gives a girth, height or circumference; girth_cm left null. Location: contest GPS (43.1618, 26.809764) sits in the town's public garden/square with a fountain, which is corroborated as 'town centre' by both independent sources but not pinned to the individual trunk by any of them, so marked approximate rather than confirmed. No hard-rule-10 issue: this is an open public square, a community gathering place, not private land.

name: The Encina de San Roque (the Spanish Oak of San Roque)

location.address: Monte de La Redonda, beside the Ermita de San Roque, Barrio San Roque, Colindres, Cantabria, Spain

access: Free, in open woodland on Monte de La Redonda beside the public Ermita de San Roque; the site hosts a World Environment Day gathering and a popular countryside festival ('fiesta campestre') each August, so it is a normal community open-air spot, not fenced or restricted.
transport: Colindres is a small town on the Cantabrian coast near Laredo; the oak is a short walk from the town's San Roque neighbourhood, reached by road/local bus from Santander (roughly 45km) or Laredo.
verify_notes: Spain's own 'Arbol y Bosque del Ano' register (arbolybosquedelano.es) gives precise measurements independent of the contest: height 16m (trunk/fuste 3.15m), girth at breast height (1.30m) 3.70m = 370cm (girth_cm set to this), and a base-of-trunk circumference of 4.40m/440cm, which a search snippet mistranslated as 'diameter' but the source page clearly labels 'Perimetro de base' (circumference). Age ~400 years agreed by contest, arbolybosquedelano.es and elasombrario.publico.es. Stands on Monte de La Redonda beside the Ermita de San Roque, overlooking what was the medieval Camino Real/Salt Route; survived regional deforestation for 18th-century galleon shipyards and appears on an 1778 salt-route map. Won Spain's national 'Arbol del Ano 2023' among 16 candidates (tied to the town's 'Green Corridor' tree-planting project) before placing 6th in European Tree of the Year 2023 (10,174 votes). GPS: contest's coordinate (43.383142, -3.4384) and an independent OSM node for 'Ermita de San Roque, Barrio San Roque, Colindres' (43.383099, -3.438213) agree within about 15-20 metres; used the OSM figure as the pin. Strong single-famous-tree candidate: real girth, real history, small town with nothing else to build a page around.

name: The Millennium Oak of Veryn

location.address: By the Church of St Michael the Archangel, Veryn village, Stryi district, Lviv region, Ukraine

access: Free, on the grounds of the village church of St Michael; the local monument is explicitly unfenced (per localhistory.org.ua) and there is a well-documented informal path for visitors, so this is open village ground, not a private site.
transport: Rural village in Stryi district, Lviv region, western Ukraine; no rail or public transport directly to the tree, reached by road from Stryi (roughly 15km) or Lviv (roughly 70km).
verify_notes: Two independent Ukrainian sources beyond the contest page (spadok.org.ua, a heritage/local-history site, and localhistory.org.ua) agree closely: pedunculate oak (Quercus robur), girth 8.5m at the trunk (girth_cm=850), height roughly 18m, growing by the Church of St Michael the Archangel in Veryn. Declared a local-significance botanical monument ('botanichna pam'yatka') in 1984; named the oldest tree in Lviv region and among the oldest in Ukraine, winning 'oldest tree of Lviv region' in the 2010 national 'Tree of Ukraine' contest before placing 8th in European Tree of the Year 2024 (8,886 votes). Local legend: Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky reportedly rested in its shade; a WWII-era story holds a sniper used the trunk's large cavity (compared to a small cave) to cover the Dniester river crossing; 1917 photographs of Ukrainian Sich Riflemen soldiers beside the tree exist and were later reproduced on a postcard. The large hollow is itself a sign of the tree's age and a documented ongoing health concern (rot), not evidence against it being alive; no source suggests it has died. GPS: contest's coordinate (49.488011, 23.990658) and an independent OSM node for the village church (49.487771, 23.990716) agree within about 25-30 metres; used the OSM figure. Ukraine sourcing note per the brief: independent, non-contest Ukrainian sourcing (local heritage/history sites, regional news) was in fact readily findable despite the war, so this is not delivered on register-only grounds; it clears the ordinary two-source bar.

name: The Kaņepju Oak

location.address: Beside the Kaņepju farmstead, roughly 1.2-1.8km northeast of Jērcēni village centre, Jērcēnu parish, Valmiera municipality, Latvia

access: Free, a signposted 'turisma apskates objekts' (tourism sightseeing object); stands beside a private farmstead but the tree itself and its approach are treated as a public heritage site, not part of the private yard.
transport: Rural Jērcēnu parish, no rail; reached by road, roughly 1.5km from Jērcēni village and about 25km from Valmiera.
verify_notes: Latvian Wikipedia and viss.lv (an independent Latvian sightseeing directory) both give girth 9.2-9.4m (girth_cm set to 940, the more frequently repeated figure) and height 16-17m, canopy spread roughly 19.5x19m. Known as the second-thickest ancient oak in both Latvia and the Baltic states. Age is genuinely disputed across sources: commonly quoted as 450-800 years, but viss.lv cites a dendrochronological study by S. Salins concluding the tree dates to around 1200-1201 AD (the time Bishop Albert entered Livonian lands), which would put it near 825 years old today; recorded both figures per the brief's conflict rule rather than picking a winner. Lightning strike (reportedly 19th century) split the trunk and created a large hollow, described as big enough for 8 people, with three openings; visitors have carved names into it since at least 1886. Won a 1933 competition (in a prominent Latvian publication) for the country's mightiest oak. Listed on Latvia's state-level register of archaeological monuments as a 'cult site' (kulta vieta), i.e. believed to be a pre-Christian sacred oak. GPS: contest coordinate (57.701539, 25.6614) and Latvian Wikipedia's own coordinate (57.70139, 25.66167) are effectively identical (within a few metres); used Wikipedia's figure. Strong single-famous-tree candidate: large, old, well documented, remote rural site with nothing else nearby.

name: The Pálffy Oak of Memories

location.address: Near the eastern edge of Zámocký park (Castle Park), a National Cultural Monument, Malacky, Bratislava region, Slovakia

access: Free, in the public Zámocký park (Castle Park) in Malacky, a well-used recreation park; the trunk itself has been fenced for protection after vandalism (per stvr.sk), but the park itself is open ground, not gated.
transport: Malacky is a separate town roughly 37-38km / 44-48 minutes by direct train from Bratislava Hlavná stanica (hourly ZSSK service), or via bus line 245; outside the ~30-minute day-trip boundary from central Bratislava, so this reads as its own place rather than a Bratislava addition (see note).
verify_notes: Two independent Slovak sources (ekopolis.sk, the contest's Slovak national-round organiser, and lesmedium.sk, a forestry trade outlet) agree: pedunculate oak (Quercus robur), trunk circumference 660cm (girth_cm=660), height 20m, crown width 31m. Won Slovakia's national 'Strom roka 2023' (Tree of the Year) with 4,201 of roughly 19,000 votes before placing 14th in European Tree of the Year 2024 (5,204 votes). Stands near the eastern edge of Zamocky park, a National Cultural Monument in Malacky, and experts estimate it predates the park itself by about 100 years, i.e. it stood before the Palffy family (who built the adjoining castle and laid out the park) arrived in Malacky in the 17th century. Story frames it as a witness to the Palffy family's arrival, Napoleonic troop movements, epidemics, fires and markets. A Slovak public broadcaster (stvr.sk) headline calls it 'the second most famous tree in Europe' and reports it had to be fenced due to vandalism. BRATISLAVA DISTANCE CHECK (per the brief): Malacky is roughly 37-38km from Bratislava by road and about 44-48 minutes by direct train (hourly ZSSK service) or bus line 245, per rome2rio/chronotrains. This exceeds the roughly 30-minute public-transport day-trip boundary CLAUDE.md uses to fold a nearby tree into an existing city page, so this should ship as ITS OWN PLACE (Malacky) under the single-famous-tree exception rather than being added to Bratislava's page. GPS: contest's coordinate (48.439075, 17.036208) sits about 365m from the park's own OSM centroid, consistent with 'near the eastern edge of the park' as sources describe it, but no independent source pins the exact trunk, so marked approximate rather than confirmed.

name: The Oak of Prince Ulrich (Oldřichův dub)

location.address: Oldřichova 49, 439 07 Peruc, Ústí nad Labem Region, Czechia (Dolní Poohří area)

access: Free, a legally protected 'památný strom' (memorial tree) beside a stream at the edge of the village, with a bench for visitors; kudyznudy.cz (the Czech national tourism board's own site) treats it as an established, freely visitable destination with no restrictions mentioned.
transport: Peruc is a village in the Louny district, Usti nad Labem region; no rail station in the village, reached by road, roughly 65km northwest of Prague and about 15km from Louny.
verify_notes: The legend checks out and is a real, old one, not invented for the contest: per Czech sources (ceskestavby.cz, quoting the medieval Chronicle of Dalimil) Prince Oldrich (Ulrich), an early-11th-century Premyslid ruler, is said to have met a washerwoman named Bozena doing laundry ('perouc pradlo', the reputed origin of the village name Peruc itself) by a stream beneath this oak around 1002, fell in love and married her; their son was Duke Bretislav I. Height 31m and trunk girth 760cm (girth_cm=760) agreed by kudyznudy.cz and ceskestavby.cz. AGE DISPUTE, recorded per the brief rather than resolved: commonly cited as roughly 1000 years and the tree is on the UNESCO list of most significant trees per kudyznudy.cz, but ceskestavby.cz itself reports some experts/foresters think this may be a YOUNGER tree onto which the legend transferred after the original oak died; age_min/age_max set widely (300-1000) to reflect that real disagreement rather than picking a winner. Survived two fires, in 1993 and 1995. Currently stands near a forest kindergarten (lesni skolka), which does not restrict public access to the tree itself. Won Czech national 'Strom roku' (Tree of the Year) 2025 before placing 7th in European Tree of the Year 2026 (2,325 points) as the newest contest year; a genuine independent second source exists well beyond the contest page (Czech national tourism board kudyznudy.cz, plus ceskestavby.cz and turistika.cz). GPS: contest coordinate (50.345, 13.962) and an independent OSM geocode of the tree's own street address, Oldřichova 49, Peruc (50.344814, 13.961542), agree within about 30-40 metres; used the address geocode.
